- If sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slightly, especially after spikes.
- If sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.50), model often underestimates; increase forecast modestly to counteract pessimism.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior day), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% above peak or adjust downward after 3–5 days.
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.00–0.33), model often fails to mean-revert; apply a gentle downward bias if price is above 30-day moving average.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome shows early sharp decline after a peak, model often lags; adjust forecast downward by 1–3% in first 5–7 days post-peak.
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative sentiment (e.g., 3+ consecutive negative values), model tends to underestimate; add 2–5% buffer to forecast.
- If model forecast is rising steadily with no sentiment reversal, consider mean reversion bias — reduce forecast slope by 10–20% if sentiment turns negative or neutral.
